correction_2026_10_09: SEPARATOR CORRECTION, 2026-10-09. Every row in this file that spelled a binding `<callable>#<binding>` now spells it with `BINDING_SEP` as the family defines it — U+0000, written `\u0000` in JSON. The character was `#` until src/ast/types.ts commit c95c8485f ("the binding separator was `#` — a character nine lanes legitimately publish, so their claims were unverifiable"): `#` is a real key character in other lanes (a CSS id selector, a markdown label, an HCL address), so `verifyBindingClaim` had to reject every binding claim on a run that also published one. The edges, their lines, their confidence and their metadata are UNCHANGED; only the separator character moved. Measured before this correction: `npx tsx script/m14/run-fixtures.ts --lang dart` -> {"dart":{"pass":21,"fail":7}}, and all 7 failures were rows whose sole difference was this character. Any `#` still visible in this file's prose is the 2026-10-08 spelling quoted as history, not the current one.
rationale: Dart's `Object` is the root of every class interface, so `toString`, `hashCode`, `runtimeType`, `noSuchMethod` and `operator ==` are reachable from every type in the language. That makes Object the ONE override target a per-file analyzer can name without the base's own file. Before this fixture the first-heritage-parent fallback named the parent instead: `class ProtocolException implements Exception` + `@override String toString()` published `ProtocolException.toString -> Exception.toString`, and `Exception` declares no `toString` at all — dart-sdk/sdk/lib/core/exceptions.dart publishes 17 symbols and `Exception.toString` is not one of them. Measured over 4,788 corpus files at BB_DART_CONC=1: 2,422 of 247,737 `overrides` rows (0.98%) named a target no published declaration provides, and every one of the 2,422 had that shape. The cases below pin the retarget AND its two boundaries, because a retarget with no boundary is indistinguishable from publishing an override for every `@override` in the corpus. (A,B,C) the retarget fires and `firstHeritageParent` preserves the name the old rule would have used, so no information is lost. (D,F) a member outside Object's five keeps the first heritage parent, and an in-file base that DOES declare the member is resolved by Pass 1 at 0.95 and never reaches the fallback. (E) an in-file base that does NOT declare the member refutes the fallback outright — asserted in forbidRelationships, because the retarget must not become a way to publish an edge where the analyzer has evidence against it. (G) naming `Object` explicitly is already correct and is not marked as a retarget. (H) is where the fix STOPS: an out-of-file base with a member outside Object's five has no declaration the analyzer can name, so the unverifiable first-parent target is KEPT at 0.8 with `isExternalBase` rather than replaced by an invented one. Case H is also what makes M2 constructible in the mutant battery — with only Object-interface members in the file, an over-broad `retarget everything onto Object` mutant is a no-op, and a no-op mutant passes every check. (I,J) a `calls` CALLEE can be a binding: freezed's generated `map`/`maybeMap` takes the mapping function as a formal parameter named `$default` and calls it, so `$default(_that)` is a real invocation whose target the family contract publishes no symbol for. `uses` already carried `isLocalRead` for this and `calls` carried nothing, so 138 `calls -> $default` and 50 `calls -> orElse` rows over 4,788 corpus files were indistinguishable from calls to undeclared methods. The tag is metadata only — no row added or removed, no confidence moved — and case J pins that a declared callee is NOT tagged, or the label stops meaning anything. THE OTHER HALF OF THE OBJECT RULE (2026-10-11). The retarget above is scoped to Object's five members, and the fixture has always FORBIDDEN `Banner.build -> Object.build` on the words "a member outside Object's five must never be retargeted onto Object" — but the FIRST-HERITAGE-PARENT fallback had no such guard, so a class that writes `extends Object` explicitly and overrides a member Object does not declare still named `Object.<member>`. `extends Object` is how a Dart file writes "no superclass" (Dart's root is implicit on every class), so this is not a base that can declare `length`; MEASURED, the shape is `class LineStarts extends Object with ListMixin<int> { @override int get length => ...; }` over dart-sdk, 128 rows, every one `isExternalBase`, and every one refuted on the one project whose checkout publishes `sdk/lib/core/object.dart` — the standing `128 external claim(s) REFUTED` clause of the lane's verdict. The fallback now SKIPS `Object` for a member outside its five and names the first REAL base (`extends`/`implements`/`with`, never a bare `uses` type mention), and publishes NOTHING when only Object is left. All 128 measured rows have a real base besides Object (46 `AnalysisDriverUnitIndex` through `implements idl.AnalysisDriverUnitIndex`, 9 `ListMixin`, 7 `SetMixin`, …), so the change names a true base on every one of them or drops the row where the in-file base proves it cannot be the target. Boundaries pinned: case K (the skip fires and the mixin is named), case L (nothing is published when Object is the only base), case M (a mentioned type is not a base), case N (with two real bases the FIRST clause wins, so a `mixins.last` off-by-one is caught), and case G is the boundary in the other direction — when the member IS one of Object's five, `Object` stays the base, because its interface is the one thing a per-file run can name with no evidence about the base. THE MEMBER SURFACE EXCLUDES CONSTRUCTORS (2026-10-12). `byName` in the override pass carried every symbol named `constructor`, so a subclass member with that name matched the base's constructor BY NAME and published at 0.95 — `CtorSub.constructor -> CtorBase.constructor` here, 2 rows on dart-sdk (`pkg/compiler/lib/src/universe/recorded_use.dart`), each refuted by the exposure watchdog. Constructors are not inherited and cannot be overridden, and the overrides oracle never carried them (`memberNamesOf` handles `method_signature` and `declaration` nodes only). Case O pins the removal; case P pins its BOUNDARY — a base getter called `constructor` IS a member, so the row survives and the fix cannot be an over-exclusion.

case H — the boundary, and since 2026-10-09 the boundary between TWO DIFFERENT CLAIMS. The base is out of this file and `build` is not one of Object's five, so no declaration is nameable without the base's own file; the target is kept rather than replaced. What changed is what the row may CLAIM about it: `isExternalBase` says the PROJECT does not contain the base, and a run that was handed no project index cannot know that — MEASURED, the same claim was refuted 16,894 times on the per-file population (production's, since `parallel-indexer.ts` PROJECT_INDEX_EXTENSIONS names only `.sol`) against 93 on the index-assisted one. So the reason is stated where it is true and is its own gate column: `baseBeyondRunScope` names the base this RUN could not reach, is not an external claim, and is never folded into `resolved`. `meta.isExternalBase: null` pins the negative — the marker must not be present, or the false claim is back.

case K — `extends Object` names the language's root, which declares exactly its five members. `length` is not one of them, so `Object` is not a nameable base for this row; the fallback skips it and names the first REAL base — the `with ListMixin<int>` clause, whose BARE name is what this pass publishes for a mixin (measured: `uses LineStarts -> ListMixin {isMixin: true}`). `ListMixin` is out of this file, so the row is the 0.8 labelled guess every other out-of-file base gets, and the reason is the bucket-3 one. Measured over dart-sdk: 128 rows had the fabricated shape, every one `isExternalBase`, every one refuted on the one project whose checkout publishes `sdk/lib/core/object.dart`.
case K, second instance — the member is spelled `operator []` and the rule is on the member, not the class: one row falls through and the other does not, in the same class.

case N — with TWO real bases the fall-through names the FIRST, in the file's own clause order. `MixinA` and `MixinB` are both out of this file, so the row is the 0.8 labelled guess with the bucket-3 reason. This is the pin a fall-through that took the mixin list's END would fail.

case I — a callee that is a formal parameter, tagged so the row is countable as a binding rather than a declaration, and (2026-10-08) SPELLED so the store cannot resolve it: a bare `$default` would be bound to any single declaration of that name in the project (`resolveRelationships` Strategy 2, which never reads this metadata)
case J — a declared callee carries NO isLocalRead. `meta.x: null` is run-fixtures' M59 convention for ABSENT, so this states the negative; the strict form could never be true for an omitted label.

case P — the NAME is a member when the BASE declares it as one. Only the constructor-symbol match was the fabrication, and this row must stay or the fix would have traded a fabricated edge for a missing true one.

This is the forbid that catches a future edit restoring the marker while every positive case still passes (the positive case pins `baseBeyondRunScope`, so the two together hold the pair apart).

the cause's reason is CHECKED, not trusted: the stated base has to BE this edge's own owner, so a marker naming any other base than the target's owner is refuted by the gate rather than counted in bucket 3. `Object` is the convenient wrong reason and the battery's M5 mutant constructs it, which is what makes this pin firable rather than a string nothing ever produces.

case K, negative side — THE PRE-FIX ROW. `extends Object with ListMixin<int>` + `@override int get length` named `Object.length`, asserting a declaration `Object` has never had. On dart-sdk that row arrived as `isExternalBase` and the gate refuted it, which is the `128 external claim(s) REFUTED` clause the fix removes. Pinned as forbidden so the regression cannot return silently, and it is what the M2 (over-retarget) mutant produces.

case L, negative side — `extends Object` and NOTHING ELSE. There is no base left to name, so no row may exist at all: an out-of-file base may be guessed, a base whose members are KNOWN and which does not declare this one may not. This is the pin an output-only mutant cannot fire (the row is absent from the output, so no transform can produce it), which is why the battery's M7 constructs it.

case M, negative side — a fall-through that walked every bare `uses` target would name a type the class merely MENTIONS. `Widgetish` appears in `MentionsOnly`'s parameter list and nowhere in its heritage; only `extends`/`implements`/`with` is a base.

case N, negative side — the SECOND mixin. `MixinB` IS a real base, so this pin is not about a wrong KIND of base but about the ORDER a fall-through must hold: first clause wins, and a `mixins.last` off-by-one lands here.
case N, negative side — the pre-fix row for the two-base class as well

case J, negative side — `$default` is not bound in `callsBoth`, so the tag must not spread to a name that merely happens to look local. Retargeted 2026-10-08 to the spelling a spread tag would now produce: the tag and the `#` spelling travel together, so a forbid on the bare form would have watched the wrong string

case O, negative side — THE FABRICATED ROW. A subclass member named `constructor` matched the base's constructor SYMBOL by name and published at 0.95; constructors are not inheritable members. Pinned as forbidden so the regression cannot return silently, and it is one of the rows the mutant battery's M7 fabricates.
